item.title: Smart, digital transformation revitalizes China's old industrial base
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
SHENYANG, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- A four-legged inspection robot showcased its agility to navigate challenging terrain as it effortlessly scaled a steep slope, while another robot fitted with flexible, articulated arms demonstrated tasks designed for hazardous high-voltage industrial environments. The robots, built and displayed by Nanjing-based YIJIAHE Technology Co., Ltd., were among the exhibits drawing attention at the 2026 Global Industrial Internet Conference in Shenyang, capital of northeast China's Liaoning Province. The three-day event, which concluded on Thursday, brought together guests from political, business, academic and other sectors to discuss innovation and development of the industrial internet. Powered by technologies involving 5G and AI, the industrial internet connects people, machines and other production resources, allowing manufacturers to better coordinate and optimize production. Northeast China is one of the country's traditional industrial bases, with deep industrial roots and a well-established industrial system. The region also faces challenges in upgrading equipment and shifting growth drivers. In recent years, smart and digital transformation has become an important part of its efforts to upgrade the manufacturing sector. The opportunities created are attracting companies from outside the region. YIJIAHE, headquartered in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, established its Northeast Asia international innovation center in Shenyang last month, focusing on the development of intelligent robots for healthcare, power and firefighting. "Liaoning boasts a wide range of industrial scenarios," said Zhang Jiachun, head of solutions at the company. "We hope to explore diversified real-world applications here and support the smart and digital transformation of the old industrial base." Local companies are also tapping into Liaoning's industrial resources. At the conference, the Liaoning branch of China Mobile displayed industrial large models for sectors that include petrochemicals, electric power and equipment manufacturing. Factories across Liaoning have accumulated large amounts of production data over the years, much of which has yet to be fully utilized, according to Tang Dianbo, deputy head of the company's industrial innovation research institute. At Genertec Shenyang Machine Tool Co., Ltd., AI is being applied directly to machining. With its self-developed numerical control system, 5G private network and industrial internet platform, AI can fine-tune the machining process in real time based on changes in materials and tool wear, automatically correct machining errors and provide early warnings of potential equipment problems. The transformation is not limited to heavy industry. At Dayang Group Co., Ltd. in Liaoning's port city of Dalian, after customers upload body measurement, fabric selection and pattern design through the company's industrial internet platform for customized clothing, its system generates production instructions and enables the production line to switch between different products with minimal adjustments. By linking measurements, design, cutting and production data, customized orders can move through the same production system, allowing the company to combine large-scale production with personalized demand. "Before the digital upgrade, even the most experienced pattern makers needed around two hours to turn measurements into a pattern. The process now takes just two seconds," said Hu Dongmei, general manager of the company, adding that a customized suit can now be completed in as few as three days. Similar applications are emerging across Liaoning, with major manufacturers working with local software service providers in areas such as equipment-failure prediction, adaptive optimization of machining processes and intelligent quality control in steel production. In April, the province launched a three-year action plan for the smart and digital transformation of manufacturing, aiming to develop more than 600 industrial 5G private network projects and cultivate 150 provincial-level industrial internet platforms by the end of 2028. Similar policy support has been introduced elsewhere in northeast China. In Jilin Province, financial incentives are provided for smart and digital transformation projects, while Heilongjiang Province has organized experts to offer one-on-one assessments for enterprises, while helping to connect companies with digital service providers. The regional push is part of China's wider development of the industrial internet. Data from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shows that the country's core industrial internet industry exceeded 1.6 trillion yuan (about 236 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, while the number of industrial 5G private networks topped 26,000. The industrial internet is now applied across all major sectors in China, with 100 advanced 5G-enabled factories meeting global leading standards, according to the ministry. These facilities reported a 25 percent increase in average production capacity, a 21 percent improvement in product quality and a 19 percent reduction in operating costs. A think tank report released at the conference said northeast China's experience in applying smart and digital technologies to its well-established heavy industrial system could provide pointers for the upgrading of other traditional industrial cities in China and offer insights for similar industrial regions elsewhere in the world. ■

item.title: Whispers of Chinese characters on ceramic glaze: A ceramic micro-calligraphy inheritor's story
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
MasterOfCrafts | Whispers of Chinese characters on ceramic glaze: A ceramic micro-calligraphy inheritor's story -Xinhua MasterOfCrafts | Whispers of Chinese characters on ceramic glaze: A ceramic micro-calligraphy inheritor's story Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-11 21:32:16 JINGDEZHEN, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- There goes an old Chinese saying that "the scenery changes with each step." This saying can be true when you look at a ceramic micro-calligraphy artwork, on which Chinese characters are written in tiny little sizes so that you can not even notice them from a distance. Micro-calligraphy, or weishu, is an age-old Chinese art that wields the traditional Chinese writing brush to produce Chinese characters of astonishing minuteness with naked vision. This art form has deep roots in antiquity, with its earliest traces found in the oracle bone inscriptions from the Western Zhou Dynasty (1046 BC-771 BC). Ceramic micro-calligraphy, which combines the delicate art with polychrome ceramic, demands high in its making as the ceramic needs to go through high-temperature firing in kiln after the writing. To create a piece, the craftsman, relying solely on his naked eyes, uses a custom fashioned brush, with ultra-fine hairs and high-temperature-resistant pigments, to paint delicate motifs directly onto the ceramic's surface, no errors or corrections allowed. When the ceramic goes through repeated firings in the kiln, even the slightest deviation in temperature control can make all previous labors in vain. Upon completion, the artwork is seen with tiny little Chinese characters interlaced with paintings, complementing each other beautifully. The art has become a treasure of traditional Chinese crafts with irreplaceable artistic values, and was inscribed as one of China's national-level intangible cultural heritages in 2014. Liu Dachuan, a 47-year-old senior craftsman from south China's Guangdong Province, has dedicated himself to the art of ceramic micro-calligraphy for decades. He can inscribe up to 163 Chinese characters on a single square centimeter of porcelain, all perfectly distinguishable under a magnifying glass. Liu has formed a modern artistic style while carrying on the traditions, and his works have won multiple widely recognized awards. "Writing micro-calligraphy with the naked eye tests not only your eyesight, but also your very soul," Liu said, adding that a machine might replicate the shapes of characters, but it could never depict the flowing spirit unique to the tip of a brush. To bring ceramic micro-calligraphy to a wider audience, Liu held solo thematic exhibitions, and further established a studio in Jingdezhen, where he formally accepts apprentices and guides them step by step in the art. He also hosts public welfare open classes and intangible cultural heritage experiencing salons, where he offers lectures on the history of micro-calligraphy to local ceramics artisans and tourists on study tours. Regarded as premium collectible art pieces, ceramic micro-calligraphy artworks have won great favor from cultural institutions and museums, collectors and art lovers across the country. Meanwhile, as craftworks embodying the charm of oriental beauty, they have also appeared in exhibitions of many foreign countries, often being selected as gifts for culture exchanges, and being collected by overseas museums. In a way, they have become artistic carriers to promote the traditional Chinese culture and the exchanges between China and the world.

item.title: China's top economic planner invites private investment in 36 projects
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) has recommended 36 investment projects to private enterprises in a bid to further stimulate private investment. These 36 projects, spanning transportation, logistics, water conservancy and energy, were presented at a recent NDRC symposium involving private enterprises and industry associations. The projects have a combined estimated investment of 61.4 billion yuan (about 9.06 billion U.S. dollars) and are expected to attract 15.6 billion yuan in private capital. They cover railways, warehousing, wind power, energy storage, charging facilities and water diversion projects, among others. Private capital can participate through wholly-owned investment, controlling stakes, or equity participation in relevant companies. The NDRC said it will make full use of its regular communication and problem-solving mechanism in working with private enterprises. It will also work with relevant parties to improve services, strengthen the supply of capital, land and other factors of production, and coordinate efforts to resolve key issues to ensure early implementation of the projects. It will also establish a regular project recommendation mechanism to expand opportunities for private enterprises to participate in high-quality projects and better facilitate private investment growth. This project recommendation endeavor comes after official data showed that fixed-asset investment in China fell 6.7 percent year on year in the first seven months of 2026, while private investment dropped by 9.4 percent. Excluding real estate development, private investment declined 5.7 percent in this period. ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Services opening-up unlocks more China opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- What makes the Chinese market an opportunity for the world? The answer is increasingly found not only in its sheer size, but also in the country's expanding strengths in services, innovation and cooperation. Part of that answer lies in the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS), the first edition in the country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, which opened its doors at Beijing's Shougang Park this week. With greater international participation, this year's event underscores the growing role of services in global trade and China's resolve and confidence in advancing high-standard opening up. Today, services have become an increasingly important engine of the global economy, accounting for 65 percent of global GDP and more than a quarter of world trade, according to UN Trade and Development. Services exports are also growing at more than twice the pace of goods exports. Meanwhile, with services now forming the bedrock of the Chinese economy, China has placed services trade high on its economic agenda. In the first seven months of 2026, China's services trade expanded 8.3 percent year on year to nearly 4.45 trillion yuan (about 656.9 billion U.S. dollars). Advancing high-quality development of services trade is a key task set out in China's 15th Five-Year Plan, which calls for efforts to ease cross-border restrictions and foster knowledge-intensive services trade. Digitalization and green development are emerging as key drivers of China's services development, with advanced technologies like AI and big data increasingly integrated into services trade. This year's CIFTIS has put innovation front and center, highlighting the latest breakthroughs and practical applications. The fair offers more than a marketplace for services. Norway, this year's guest country of honor, presents a 260-square-meter pavilion featuring a wide range of exhibits, providing a platform for Norwegian companies to pursue practical cooperation in China. For U.S. pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly, the fair means opportunities to tap China's policy and research strengths and become more deeply integrated into the country's pharmaceutical innovation ecosystem, according to Huzur Devletsah, the company's vice president and China general manager. The opportunities created by China's expanding services market do not come at the expense of others: as the sector opens further, its growing capacity is opening up new avenues for international cooperation and shared growth. Reflecting this trend, this year's CIFTIS debuts an exhibition of over 140 cases spanning 12 categories of services trade, including those involving AI, large language models and intelligent agents, offering a glimpse of where China's services sector is headed. The fair also sets up a new roadshow area that provides Chinese companies with one-stop professional support to expand their global footprint in services. The country's expanding services capacity is also bringing tangible development opportunities to the Global South. According to Zimbabwean Vice President Constantino Chiwenga, the CIFTIS is expected to help his country identify opportunities for trade in services, build export capacity, and attract credible partners in areas of technology, finance, tourism, education and health care. As services become an increasingly important arena for global economic cooperation, China's continued opening-up is creating more channels for businesses around the world to connect, cooperate and grow. The "China opportunities" offered by a more open services market are becoming part of a broader landscape of shared growth. ■

item.title: China lodges solemn representations with Italy, EU over DPP official's visit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China has lodged solemn representations with Italy and the EU over the visit of "Taiwan independence" politicians to Italy for a conference, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Friday. Mao made the remarks at a regular press briefing when asked to comment on Taiwan's Hsiao Bi-khim's visit to Italy. "The Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities and certain politicians are resorting to all manner of tricks to seek publicity," Mao said. Noting that they seek independence by colluding with external forces under the pretext of "democracy" and "freedom," Mao said such acts are contemptible and will ultimately prove futile. Mao stressed that there is only one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory. China has always firmly opposed any form of official exchanges between countries that have established diplomatic ties with China and China's Taiwan region, Mao said. Mao said the one‑China principle is a universally recognized norm in international relations and the common consensus of the international community. It also constitutes the political foundation of China‑Italy relations and China‑EU relations, she added. "We urge the relevant parties to honour the one‑China principle with concrete actions," the spokesperson said. ■

item.title: China issues regulations to improve management of local market regulators
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating regulations to strengthen the management of local market regulatory authorities nationwide. The regulations will help them better perform their duties. The 19-article regulations, which call for streamlining local market regulatory mechanisms and optimizing the staffing of local market regulatory authorities, will take effect on Nov. 1. According to the regulations, such authorities' duties include registering self-employed individuals within their respective administrative areas, conducting routine oversight of food production and sales, handling market complaints, and cracking down on irregularities. Highlighting the need to improve services and foster a favorable business environment, the regulations stipulate that local market regulatory authorities must conduct regulatory activities in accordance with the law and make every effort to minimize disruption to market entities' normal production and operations. Authorities should also strengthen communication with market entities and consumers, ensure transparency in their work, and provide standardized, convenient and efficient administrative services, according to the regulations. Safeguarding fair market competition has remained high on China's development agenda, as the country places greater emphasis on building a unified national market and fostering a favorable business environment. To this end, the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for greater efforts to improve market regulatory rules, unify standards and enhance regulatory capabilities, thereby fostering a market order characterized by high quality, reasonable prices and healthy competition. ■

item.title: China, India are making arrangements for Xi-Modi meeting, says spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China and India are making arrangements for a meeting between President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the upcoming 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Friday. This will mark the third consecutive year in which Xi and Modi meet, following their meetings in Kazan and Tianjin, said Mao Ning, the spokesperson, at a regular news briefing. She said China stands ready to work with India to follow the strategic guidance of the two leaders, view bilateral relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, strengthen communication, expand cooperation, and properly handle differences, so as to be good-neighborly friends and partners helping each other succeed. ■

item.title: From Bishkek to New Delhi, Xi advocates Global South cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping is heading to New Delhi for this year's BRICS gathering just over a week after he took part in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek. The two back-to-back multilateral engagements converge on a single, defining theme: galvanizing solidarity and cooperation across the Global South. EXPANDING FAMILY The SCO "takes root in the Global South, its heart beats with the Global South, and it is an important pillar of South-South cooperation," Xi said at the Bishkek summit concluded on Tuesday last week, calling on the SCO to "promote the development and rise of the Global South through the SCO Wisdom." The Chinese leader is expected to put forward further proposals on Global South cooperation at the upcoming BRICS summit, as he has noted that the BRICS is "standing at the forefront of the Global South." This year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO and the 20th anniversary of the BRICS cooperation mechanism, both milestone occasions. Riding the wave of the collective rise of the Global South, BRICS and the SCO have over the years expanded their membership and broadened their networks of developing partners. Their members jointly account for more than half of the world's population and about 30 percent of the global economy. This illustrates the fact that the two groupings have evolved into major platforms for Global South cooperation. Xi has not only joined other leaders of member countries in pushing for their respective expansions, but also put forward new ideas and initiatives like the "BRICS Plus" cooperation approach and the building of an SCO community with a shared future, opening up new vistas for win-win cooperation among Global South countries. "China has consistently provided a clear vision and momentum for BRICS and the SCO, both conceptually and practically," said Humprey Arnaldo Russel, head of the ASEAN-China Research Center at the University of Indonesia. "It transformed BRICS from a relatively exclusive grouping into a broader platform for cooperation among developing countries and the wider Global South," he added. DEVELOPMENT FIRST At the SCO summit last week, Xi called on countries to "stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity." Amid a turbulent and rapidly changing international landscape, development still faces severe challenges, and the road to prosperity for the Global South will not be straight. "The Global South emerges for development and prospers through development. We should make ourselves the main driving force for common development," Xi said during the 2024 BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia. For Xi, development has always been a priority. He sees it as "the master key to solving all problems," and has consistently called for countries worldwide to jointly pursue development and prosperity. Xi has stressed repeatedly that no one should be left behind in the fight against poverty in China, and has led a formidable campaign that ended extreme poverty nationwide, which was hailed as "the greatest anti-poverty achievement in history." His "leaving-no-one-behind" conviction also extends to his efforts to support poverty reduction and spur development across the Global South. "On the path to modernization, no one, and no country, should be left behind," Xi said. Last week in Bishkek, Xi called for consolidating cooperation in both traditional and emerging fields, from trade, investment, connectivity and energy to artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy and green industries. Responding to the Global South's aspirations for common development and modernization, Xi has proposed the Global Development Initiative (GDI), which marks its fifth anniversary this year. In the last five years, the GDI has mobilized more than 23 billion U.S. dollars, provided support for over 1,800 "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, and sponsored training programs for more than 200,000 people in different professions. Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper, said: "Under Xi's leadership, the concept of development has acquired a new international dimension and become part of a broader vision for humanity's shared future." GREATER VOICE As the Global South rises, it deserves a bigger say in global affairs. Last year's SCO Tianjin summit witnessed Xi's proposal of the Global Governance Initiative, a major proposition of China to advance a more just and equitable global governance system. At the heart of this vision is the conviction that every country has a place and an equal role to play in global governance. Xi has long argued that international affairs should not be dictated by those with more muscles. "World affairs should be discussed by all, and international norms should be set by all," he said in Bishkek last week. "The domination of international affairs by a few is an injustice left over from history, and global governance dictated by one, a few or a bloc of countries is not true multilateralism." "As an important part of a multipolar world and a key driving force behind it, the Global South countries ought to have greater representation and voice in international affairs," Xi said. Over the years, the SCO and BRICS have grown into vital venues for Global South countries to articulate their interests, coordinate their positions and strengthen their collective influence. Their growing role can be seen in political coordination. The two groupings have issued statements on international and regional hotspot issues. In March this year, for example, SCO member states issued a statement expressing grave concern over developments in the Middle East and the strikes on Iran. Xi has also pushed for improving global economic and financial governance. In 2014, Xi and other BRICS leaders formally signed an agreement establishing the New Development Bank, creating a new channel for financing infrastructure and sustainable development in emerging markets and developing countries. At the SCO Bishkek summit, the members reaffirmed the importance of establishing the SCO Development Bank. Now the push for a greater say is extending into emerging areas that will shape the future. In July this year, Xi announced the creation of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, and called for joint efforts to build a just and equitable system of global AI governance. "We must carry out extensive international cooperation and help Global South countries with capacity building to bridge the AI and digital divides, promote sustainable development, and prevent creating new historical injustice in AI," Xi said. Beyond the SCO and BRICS, China has also promoted cooperation and greater representation for the Global South through frameworks such as the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation and the China-ASEAN summit. Xi has said on many occasions that China has always been a member of the Global South and will always belong to the developing world. "No matter how the international landscape evolves, we in China will always keep the Global South in our heart, and maintain our roots in the Global South," he once said.■
